DROP (no brief, review: FULL): the commit is a 3-line treewide fix (numstat 0/4 + 2/2 + 1/1) that only rewrites bare 'totalram_pages' to 'totalram_pages()', and none of its three target lines exist in sdm670. (1) drivers/gpu/arm/ is not tracked in sdm670 at all - the Exynos Mali bv_r38p1 driver is absent, and our tree already reads totalram_pages() with no KERNEL_VERSION(5,0,0) block; (2) drivers/staging/android/ion/ion.c has no totalram_pages at HEAD; (3) mm/memblock.c has no totalram_pages and no memsize_reserved_show/kernel_mem_reg at HEAD. include/linux/mm.h:47 already defines totalram_pages as a static inline function, and the only bare users left tree-wide are drivers/parisc/sba_iommu.c:1414 (not built on arm64) plus comments. Taking theirs anywhere would have imported ~165 lines of unrelated Samsung memblock debugfs code and ~18 lines of Samsung ION heap/flag checks that this commit does not add - the same borrowed-base-context trap as CONFIG_NETPM and KNOX NPA

DROP (no brief, review: FULL), follows skipped 7f4178e8fe70: the commit's entire content is the deletion of the single line 'ccflags-y += -O3' from the zstd 1.5.x-layout lib/zstd/Makefile that 7f4178e8fe70 'BACKPORT: lib: zstd: Upgrade to version 1.4.10' creates (skip group in conflict_detail.tsv). The whole conflict block is the object-list layout difference: ours lists the flat objects (fse_compress.o huf_compress.o compress.o), theirs lists the new subdirectory objects (common/*.o compress/*.o). REVIEWER NOTE: our lib/zstd/Makefile does still carry 'ccflags-y += -O3' at line 4, so unlike the rest of this chain the one line the commit deletes could have been applied to our file in isolation. I dropped it instead, because it is a tuning change belonging to the zstd version upgrade we are deliberately not taking, and taking one piece of a skipped chain leaves the tree in no version's state. Reversing this DROP is a one-line deletion if the reviewer wants it. 5 further lib/zstd commits are expected to drop the same way

Two of its three conflicting files (lib/zstd/common/entropy_common.c, lib/zstd/common/zstd_common.c) do not exist in sdm670 (verified with git cat-file -e a30605a54f3b), and lib/zstd/Makefile conflicts because the object list is the 1.5.x subdirectory layout created by the skipped upgrade. The third file, lib/Kconfig, auto-merged and would have added 'config ZSTD_COMMON' plus two 'select ZSTD_COMMON' lines; --skip discards that too, which is correct, because nothing in sdm670's flat zstd would ever use the new symbol and leaving it in Kconfig with no obj-$(CONFIG_ZSTD_COMMON) target would be dead config. 4 further lib/zstd commits are expected to drop the same way

DROP (no brief, review: FULL): pure rewrite of CAF base machinery that sdm670 does not have - the entire diff only manipulates a 'force_scan' variable, and this tree has no force_scan anywhere (verified 'git show HEAD:mm/vmscan.c | grep -c force_scan' = 0, and 0 hits for force_scan/some_scanned anywhere in mm/ or include/). The commit replaces 'if (current_is_kswapd()) { if (!pgdat_reclaimable(pgdat)) force_scan = true; if (!mem_cgroup_online(memcg)) force_scan = true; } if (!global_reclaim(sc)) force_scan = true;' with 'if (!global_reclaim(sc) || !mem_cgroup_online(memcg)) force_scan = true;' plus a comment reword, i.e. 5 insertions / 14 deletions confined to that one if-statement and the comment above it. There is nothing to port. (1) The first half of the commit removes a '!pgdat_reclaimable(pgdat)' restriction on kswapd; sdm670 has no such restriction to remove - it has pgdat_reclaimable_PAGES() at mm/vmscan.c:233 (a page count, declared include/linux/swap.h:326) but no pgdat_reclaimable() predicate at all, so the construct being deleted does not exist here. (2) The second half makes the offline-memcg force_scan apply outside kswapd; sdm670 already behaves that way unconditionally - its equivalent is the in-loop clause 'if (!scan && !mem_cgroup_online(memcg)) scan = min(lruvec_size, SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX);' at mm/vmscan.c:2476, which I have kept through every conflict in this memcg run precisely because it is sdm670's form of the force_scan mechanism, and it contains no current_is_kswapd() test, so deleted cgroups are already scraped by both kswapd and direct reclaim. The only current_is_kswapd() in that neighbourhood is mm/vmscan.c:2541 ('scan_adjusted = (global_reclaim(sc) && !current_is_kswapd() && ...'), which is unrelated proportional scan adjustment. (3) Nothing is deleted by dropping: the code this commit modifies is absent from sdm670, so its behaviour is preserved exactly rather than reverted - this is not the 'delete code to silence an error' pattern the rules forbid. (4) This is the series' first commit that touches CAF's force_scan/two-pass reclaim directly, and it confirms the conclusion I reached while resolving fe1a3a244e241: that machinery (force_scan, some_scanned, pass, the 'for (pass = 0; !some_scanned && pass < 2; pass++)' loop, pgdat_reclaimable gating) is CAF BASE in the Exy tree, not content the ExyHyperBrick series delivers - 'git log exy/lineage-23.2 -S'some_scanned' -- mm/vmscan.c' returns only 6f04f48dc9c0 and its CAF backport 1c225cfcb958, and neither SHA is a member of analysis/exyhyperbrick-trial/results.tsv. Expect the sibling commit 1c225cfcb958 (next in the series, 'BACKPORT: mm: don't avoid high-priority reclaim on memcg limit reclaim') to be the same shape. For the reviewer: this DROP is safe precisely BECAUSE I kept sdm670's own offline-cgroup scrape clause at every one of those conflicts instead of replacing it with CAF's force_scan form; had I taken theirs verbatim earlier, this commit would then have had something to rewrite and the two would have had to be resolved together

DROP (no brief, review: FULL): THE SUBJECT FUNCTION DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS TREE. This commit is a race fix entirely inside SYSCALL_DEFINE2(process_mrelease) - it changes 'bool reap = true' to 'false', replaces the unconditional 'mm = p->mm; atomic_inc(&mm->mm_count);' with 'if (mmget_not_zero(p->mm))', and replaces the 'drop_mm: mmdrop(mm);' label body with 'if (mm) mmput(mm);'. sdm670 has no process_mrelease at all: 'grep -rn process_mrelease --include=*.c --include=*.h' over the whole tree returns only this commit's own conflict markers, and there is no process_mrelease function anywhere in mm/oom_kill.c (the only functions in that region are pagefault_out_of_memory at :1092, add_to_oom_reaper at :1107 and the __oom_reap_task_mm call at :1176). There is nothing to fix and nothing to resolve. (1) WHY IT IS MISSING, and this is the real finding: the three commits that introduce process_mrelease were all skipped by a DEFECT IN THE CLASSIFIER, not by a considered decision. They are 2e700093ca33 'mm, oom: Share address-space reaping with process_mrelease', e987691659c0 'BACKPORT: mm: introduce process_mrelease system call' and 996b9f83a3fa 'BACKPORT: mm: wire up syscall process_mrelease' - all three are group=skip in analysis/exyhyperbrick-trial/conflict_detail.tsv, and all three trip the same false positive I already found and documented earlier this run: analysis/exyhyperbrick-trial/classify.py:35 builds SKIP with re.compile(r'...|EAS|...', re.I) with no word boundary, so the substring 'eas' matches inside 'proc-EAS-s' and 'rel-EAS-e'. Verified directly - grepping 'eas' case-insensitively hits in all three subjects. So a pure substring collision silently removed an entire Android feature. (2) WHY THIS COMMIT REACHED THE CONFLICT INSTEAD OF BEING SKIPPED: unlike the trio, 030886f39a44 is marked CLEAN in analysis/exyhyperbrick-trial/results.tsv (line 2595), so it has NO row in conflict_detail.tsv, hence no group, hence pick-series.sh does not skip it - it was picked normally and only then failed, because its prerequisite is absent. So the classifier bug produced the worst combination: the commits that WOULD have been skipped are gone, and the commit that depends on them is not. (3) WHY I AM DROPPING RATHER THAN BACKTRACKING TO PICK THE TRIO - this is an escalation, not a judgement I should make unilaterally. Porting process_mrelease is real work, not a conflict resolution: 2e700093ca33 is +50/-37 and e987691659c0 is +71, both confined to mm/oom_kill.c, and a 4.9 adaptation is required. Concretely, this tree has NO mmap_lock API at all - 'grep -rn mmap_read_lock|mmap_write_lock|mmap_write_unlock define mmap_sem include/linux/mm.h' returns nothing, because sdm670 is still on the 4.9 mmap_sem rw_semaphore accessed via down_read/up_read directly - whereas the process_mrelease code is written against mmap_read_lock/mmap_write_lock and the MMF_OOM_VICTIM-flag protocol for blocking exit_mmap. MMF_OOM_SKIP, HOWEVER, DOES exist in this tree - it is at include/linux/sched.h:618 ('#define MMF_OOM_SKIP 21'), not mm_types.h as I first wrote in this row; I had grepped only include/linux/mm_types.h and wrongly concluded it was absent. sdm670's __oom_reap_task_mm already tests it (mm/oom_kill.c, 'if (test_bit(MMF_OOM_SKIP, &mm->flags))'), so the port would NOT need a new mm flag. The other half of that claim does hold and is the real porting cost: there is no mmap_lock API in this tree at all (0 hits for mmap_read_lock/mmap_write_lock/mmap_read_unlock/mmap_write_unlock), and struct mm_struct still carries 'rw_semaphore mmap_sem' at include/linux/mm_types.h:438, so the mm locking in process_mrelease must be rewritten onto mmap_sem. 996b9f83a3fa additionally has to wire the syscall number through arch/arm/tools/syscall.tbl, arch/arm64/include/asm/unistd.h, arch/arm64/include/asm/unistd32.h, include/uapi/asm-generic/unistd.h, include/linux/syscalls.h and kernel/sys_ni.c, and the wire-up is the part most likely to collide with P3's syscall work. None of that is in scope for 'resolve the conflict you are stopped on'. (4) SAFE TO DROP, not a silent feature regression that breaks the build: nothing in this tree references process_mrelease, so removing the commit leaves the tree exactly as it was and introduces no link or compile error. The user-visible consequence is that Android's lmkd calling process_mrelease gets ENOSYS; AOSP lmkd treats that as an error and falls back to an ordinary kill, so low-memory killing still works, just with less proactive memory release. I have NOT verified that fallback claim against the actual LineageOS 23.2 lmkd source - that check needs the userspace tree, which P1 does not have - which is exactly why this is being escalated rather than decided. (5) ESCALATION for the lead - recommend a decision before the port is declared done, because this is a user-visible feature, not a build blocker: either (a) authorise a follow-up pick of the chain in series order 2e700093ca33 -> e987691659c0 -> 030886f39a44 -> e0c1326972d7 -> 996b9f83a3fa, budgeting a genuine 4.9 port of the mm locking and the MMF_OOM_SKIP flag, or (b) accept the ENOSYS fallback and record the classifier defect as the root cause. Option (a) is the right call IF the target userspace's lmkd relies on process_mrelease. Either way the underlying bug is the same one already recorded for the fuse-bpf pair (f83e432ae342, ed409e286013): classify.py:35 needs \b around the EAS alternative, and every other skip-group row needs re-checking against the corrected regex, not just these three.

DROP (no brief, review: FULL): the single line this commit changes lives inside SYSCALL_DEFINE2(process_mrelease, ...), which does not exist in this tree - same root cause as the 030886f39a44 drop two stops ago. The whole diff is 1 insertion / 1 deletion in mm/oom_kill.c: 'drop_mm: if (mm) mmput(mm);' becomes 'mmput_async(mm);', and the 'drop_mm:' label only exists in the process_mrelease syscall. Verified absent: 'grep -rn process_mrelease --include=*.c --include=*.h' over the whole tree returns no definition (the only hits anywhere are conflict markers in transient worktree states), and mm/oom_kill.c has no process_mrelease function. (1) Note the commit's own message states it is a 4.9-specific backport by Mathias Gluszczynski ('The 4.9 backport pins mm_users to serialize page-table destruction with process_mrelease ... Use the existing mmput_async helper, as the 4.9 OOM reaper already does'), i.e. it is explicitly written against a tree that HAS process_mrelease. This tree does not, so the premise of the commit does not hold here and there is nothing to apply. (2) The behaviour it describes is not reachable on sdm670 by any other route: the hazard is the process_mrelease caller holding the final mm reference and inheriting exit_aio and other slow teardown when it drops that reference. With no such caller, and with sdm670's own __oom_reap_task_mm already using mmput_async for the reaper path as the commit's message notes, there is no remaining path for this fix to affect. (3) Same escalation as recorded for 030886f39a44 - this is the second commit dropped solely because the classifier's EAS substring bug (analysis/exyhyperbrick-trial/classify.py:35, 'EAS' with no word boundary, matching inside 'proc-EAS-s'/'rel-EAS-e') removed 2e700093ca33, e987691659c0 and 996b9f83a3fa, so process_mrelease was never introduced. Note that this commit e0c1326972d75 is NOT itself in the skip group - it is marked CLEAN in results.tsv (line 2597) so pick-series.sh picked it and it only failed at apply time, exactly like 030886f39a44. If the lead later authorises picking the process_mrelease chain (2e700093ca33 -> e987691659c0 -> 030886f39a44 -> e0c1326972d75 -> 996b9f83a3fa), this commit must be re-applied then; it is recorded here as dropped solely for that reason and is NOT judged to be wrong in itself. (4) Safe for the build: nothing in this tree references process_mrelease, so skipping leaves the tree exactly as it was.
